conditions.description: Host has no usable bwrap and the caller left backend at the default 'auto'.

confidence.reason: Direct source trace; behavior confirmed in code.

description: When the sandbox backend request is 'auto' (the default), resolve_backend returns caps.preferred, which is 'process' on hosts without a usable bwrap. The run then executes tool effects with process-level isolation instead of bubblewrap (read-only host view, no network namespace, seccomp denylist) — with no warning at the decision point. The downgrade is documented in the module docstring and an explicit 'bwrap' request fails closed, so this is a documented design tradeoff, not a hidden bypass.

execution.attacker_perspective: A local operator (or a misconfigured deployment) assumes bubblewrap-grade isolation because the sandbox is 'on', while effects actually run with process-level isolation.
instructions: Run any shell tool with the default sandbox request on a host where bwrap is not installed.
Observe via SandboxCapabilities that preferred resolved to 'process'.
execution.observed_result: Effects run without the read-only host bind, network namespace unsharing, or seccomp denylist that the bwrap path provides.
payloads: backend='auto' (default) on a host without bwrap

intended_behavior: The operator-visible isolation level should match what was requested, or the downgrade should be explicit at the decision point.

remediation.strategy: Emit an explicit, auditable notice when 'auto' downgrades (e.g. a warning record in the run transcript / audit feed), or add a strict mode where 'auto' fails closed instead of downgrading. Smallest change: log the resolved backend at the decision point in run_sandboxed.

root_cause: resolve_backend maps 'auto' to caps.preferred without distinguishing 'operator chose weaker isolation' from 'stronger isolation unavailable'.

impact.reason: Weaker isolation is still the documented 'process' backend, not an escape; no boundary is crossed beyond the documented tradeoff.

likelihood.reason: Requires a host without bwrap plus an operator who assumed bwrap-grade isolation; the downgrade is documented.

title: Sandbox backend 'auto' silently downgrades to the weaker 'process' backend when bwrap is unavailable

trace.description: 'auto' returns caps.preferred without checking which backend that is.
preferred is 'bwrap' only when usable, else 'process'.
Tool effects execute under the resolved (possibly downgraded) backend.

conditions.description: A future or third-party caller passes a non-dict payload without the adjacent isinstance/dict() guards present in today's callers.

confidence.reason: Branch confirmed in source and by direct execution; unreachability verified by tracing all four production callers.

description: digest_arguments (permissions.py:106-124) digests `arguments if isinstance(arguments, dict) else {}`: any non-dict payload (list, string, int) produces the same digest as an empty argument object, with no error. In every production path this branch is currently unreachable-with-divergence — ActionGateway.execute rejects non-dict before digesting, and PermissionEngine.evaluate's dict(payload or {}) raises inside the fail-closed callback guard — so no approval can be detached from its arguments today. The branch is a latent footgun: a future caller that digests without the adjacent type check would bind approvals to a digest that does not describe the real arguments.

evidence.description: Call site passes `payload or {}` where payload is only annotation-typed dict|None.

execution.attacker_perspective: Not directly exploitable today; this is a defense-in-depth observation about a silent-coercion branch at a security boundary.
instructions: Call digest_arguments with a non-dict payload.
Observe it returns the {} digest instead of raising.
execution.observed_result: A valid-looking sha256: digest that describes {} rather than the actual payload.
payloads: digest_arguments([1, 2]) == digest_arguments({})  # True, confirmed by local execution

intended_behavior: The digest function should either guarantee it only ever sees dict|None (and say so) or raise on anything else, so a type error can never silently become a valid-looking binding.

remediation.strategy: Replace the silent coercion with an explicit rejection: raise ValueError on non-dict, non-None input. Smallest change is two lines in digest_arguments plus a regression test asserting the raise.

root_cause: Defensive coercion (`else {}`) chosen over loud failure at the digest boundary.

impact.reason: No demonstrated boundary crossing; the observation is a latent hardening gap.

likelihood.reason: Unreachable with divergence in all current production callers; requires a new caller without adjacent guards.

title: digest_arguments silently coerces non-dict payloads to the {} digest instead of failing loudly

trace.description: Public digest helper; the else-branch coerces non-dict to {}.
sha256 of the coerced canonical JSON is returned as the binding.

claimed_root_cause: Silent {} coercion in digest_arguments combined with digest comparison at execution time.
description: Candidate claimed that because digest_arguments coerces non-dict payloads to the {} digest, an approval bound at one (call, digest) pair could authorize a later call with different non-dict arguments, since both digests would collide at sha256({}).

evidence.description: `if not isinstance(arguments, dict): raise ValueError('tool arguments must be an object')` — non-dict never reaches the digest comparison.

`dict(payload or {})` raises TypeError for truthy non-dict payloads inside the fail-closed `except Exception` guard; falsy non-dict ([]) is consistently treated as {} by both the digest and the callback.

reason: Refuted by source trace: every production path that binds or checks the digest either type-checks dict first (action_gateway.execute) or fails closed on non-dict (permissions.evaluate's callback guard). The two digests being compared can only collide when both sides saw the same coerced value, in which case the call was already denied before execution. No boundary crossing demonstrated.
title: Hypothesis: a non-dict tool payload could replay an approval onto different arguments

trace.description: Digest pinned before the host callback.
Execution-time digest compared against the call's bound digest.
